name: One Aldwych
positioning: Independent hotel in a 1905 Edwardian building in Covent Garden, with a 400-strong contemporary art collection
best_for: Theatre-goers who want to walk to West End shows
Guests who need dairy- and gluten-free dining

facts.text: The building was built in 1905 as the home of the Morning Post newspaper.
One Aldwych opened as a hotel in 1998.
The building was designed by the architects Mewes and Davis, known for the Ritz in Paris and London.
The hotel is home to a 400-strong collection of contemporary art and sculptures.
One Aldwych is within a ten-minute walk of over twenty West End theatres.
The hotel is moments from the Royal Opera House, The National Gallery and Somerset House.
Indigo, the signature restaurant, uses British ingredients from independent producers.
The hotel serves an afternoon tea inspired by Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.
Rooms include a complimentary curated minibar and a Nespresso coffee machine.
Hotel guests have 24-hour access to the gym.
Families can book up to four interconnecting rooms.
The Terrace signature suite is set up for private al fresco dining with views over London's rooftops.

highlights.text: The Morning Post's printing presses were once in the basement, where the hotel's swimming pool now sits.
The lap pool, hidden under the hotel, is chlorine-free thanks to a mineral cleaning system.
The Dome signature suite has a bedroom beneath the dome of the Art Nouveau building.
Indigo's menu is entirely dairy- and gluten-free.
The hotel's Curators, local experts, share guest experiences such as a historic walking tour and meeting the casts of a West End theatre.

considerations.text: Dogs must be small to medium-sized, over one year old and house-trained, and stay in dedicated dog-friendly rooms; tell the hotel when booking.
WhataHotel notes the busy central London location may bring street noise.
